title_en: Yining Huaqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. v. High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region — dispute over enforcement ruling
ruling_gist_en: First, a mediation statement that has taken effect in accordance with the law not only confirms the content of the rights and obligations agreement reached by the parties on a voluntary and lawful basis, but also is a legally binding document with compulsory enforcement effect.
keywords_en: civil; enforcement objection; dispute over sales contract; enforcement supervision; Supreme People's Court; Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; legal person; natural person; Civil Procedure Law; enforceability of mediation statement; procedure for determining liability for breach of contract; dismissal of petition; performance of mediation statement; dispute over liability for breach of contract
full_text_en:
Yining Huaqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. v. High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region — dispute over enforcement of mediation agreement

[Ruling Summary]

1. A legally effective mediation agreement not only confirms the content of the rights and obligations agreement reached by the parties on a voluntary and lawful basis, but also constitutes a legally enforceable instrument.

2. The content determined by a legally effective instrument that may be subject to compulsory enforcement must be of a nature capable of being performed. If one party fails to perform in accordance with the determined content, the other party may apply to the people's court for compulsory enforcement in respect of that determined content. Therefore, when accepting an enforcement case, the people's court shall first examine whether the applicant's claim for the creditor's right exists, that is, it has the authority to examine whether the mediation agreement or other legal instrument is enforceable. Such examination primarily includes verifying whether the legal instrument has taken legal effect, whether the obligor has performed the obligation within the time limit determined by the legal instrument, and whether the conditions for compulsory enforcement determined by the legal instrument are clear.

3. The obligation to pay arising from the liability for breach of contract by both parties, as determined in a legally effective instrument such as a mediation agreement, depends on future events, i.e., whether and to what extent the parties have breached the agreement during the performance of the effective mediation agreement. Such an obligation constitutes a new substantive dispute over rights and obligations that arises in connection with new facts occurring after the conclusion of the case. It is not a simple factual determination, and direct determination in the enforcement proceedings lacks procedural legitimacy and necessary procedural safeguards. In order to more effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of all parties, the parties should be permitted to resolve the matter through a separate action.

Supreme People's Court Enforcement Ruling

(2014) Zhi Jian Zi No. 80

Petitioner (Enforcement Applicant): Yining Huaqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 136 Fuzhou Road, Yining Border Economic Cooperation Zone (Second Floor, Building 7, Jincheng Jiayuan, Yining City).

Legal Representative: Wang Hua, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wu Fan, Attorney at Law, Xinjiang Yili Jia Law Firm.

Respondent (Enforcement Respondent): Li Zhengbo, male, Han Chinese, residing in Yining City, Xinjiang.

Agent ad litem: Li Jun, Attorney at Law, Xinjiang Tongji Law Firm.

The petitioner, Yining Huaqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaqiang Company), being dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Xin Zhi Er Jian Zi No. 148 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, filed a petition with this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct a review. On June 13, 2014, this Court held a hearing, which was attended by the legal representative and agent ad litem of Huaqiang Company, as well as Li Zhengbo and his agent ad litem. The review of this case has now been concluded.

Upon review, this Court finds the following facts: In the case of dispute over a sales contract between Huaqiang Company and Li Zhengbo, the Yining City People's Court rendered the Civil Mediation Agreement (2010) Yi Min Chu Zi No. 1514 on May 25, 2010, the main contents of which were as follows: 1. The defendant, Li Zhengbo, shall supply to the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, 13.5 million sintered porous bricks from May 1, 2010, to November 31, 2010 (including 1.5 million bricks in May, 2.7 million bricks each month from June to August, 1.7 million bricks each month from September to October, and 500,000 bricks in November), at a unit price of RMB 0.36 per brick. The defendant shall be responsible for transportation (within the scope of Yining City, with the transport location to be notified by the plaintiff one day in advance). In addition, when the stock of bricks in each kiln exceeds one ring, the plaintiff shall pay RMB 0.015 for each excess brick; 2. If the defendant, Li Zhengbo, is unable to complete the monthly supply of bricks as agreed, he must make up the shortfall in the following month. If the shortfall is still not made up in the following month, he shall compensate the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, at RMB 0.29 per brick for the shortfall; 3. The plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, shall settle accounts with the defendant, Li Zhengbo, on the 30th day of each month and pay the full amount for the bricks purchased that month within five working days. For overdue payment, a penalty of 0.05% per day shall be borne. The defendant, Li Zhengbo, shall provide a total of RMB 2,000,000 in state-recognized tax invoices (general invoices); 4. The defendant, Li Zhengbo, may sell bricks on his own only after completing the monthly supply of bricks as agreed, and the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, shall not obstruct such sales. During the supply period, the defendant shall not contact the plaintiff's customers for settlement; 5. Both parties shall strictly perform the above agreement. If the plaintiff fails to pay as agreed, it shall bear a penalty of 30% of the unpaid portion. If the defendant fails to supply sufficient bricks, in addition to compensating the plaintiff at RMB 0.29 per brick, he shall also bear a penalty of 30% of the shortfall; 6. The parties have no other disputes. The case acceptance fee of RMB 4,828 and postal fee of RMB 60 shall be borne by the plaintiff in the amount of RMB 3,000 and by the defendant in the amount of RMB 1,888.

Li Zhengbo performed in accordance with the content determined by the above mediation agreement until June 2010 but then failed to continue performance. Huaqiang Company applied to the Yining City People's Court for enforcement on July 3, 2010, and September 6, 2010, respectively, requesting Li Zhengbo to perform the obligation of supplying bricks as determined by the mediation agreement. Li Zhengbo also made related requests to the Yining City People's Court for the performance of the obligation determined by the mediation agreement. The court organized consultations between the parties. Li Zhengbo subsequently applied for retrial to the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region on July 16, 2010, requesting the revocation of the Civil Mediation Agreement (2010) Yi Min Chu Zi No. 1514 of the Yining City People's Court. On April 6, 2011, the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered the Civil Ruling (2010) Yi Zhou Min Shen Zi No. 157, dismissing Li Zhengbo's application for retrial. On April 25, 2011, Li Zhengbo applied for retrial to the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. On November 26, 2012, the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered the Civil Ruling (2012) Xin Min Shen Zi No. 1210, dismissing Li Zhengbo's application for retrial.

On May 20, 2011, Huaqiang Company applied to the Yining City People's Court for enforcement, requesting the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, to pay liquidated damages of RMB 4,350,326.94 and late performance damages of RMB 520,000. On January 9, 2012, the Yining City People's Court accepted the case for enforcement. On January 11, 2012, the Yining City People's Court issued the Enforcement Notice (2012) Yi Zhi Zi No. 31 to the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, notifying Li Zhengbo to perform the obligation of paying RMB 4,350,326.94 to Huaqiang Company within three days and to bear an enforcement application fee of RMB 45,903. Because the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, failed to perform the obligation of paying the case amount in accordance with the enforcement notice, the Yining City People's Court rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2012) Yi Zhi Zi No. 31 on February 27, 2012, with the following contents: Freeze and transfer the deposits of the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, in the amount of RMB 4,396,229.94; attach and withhold the income of the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, in the amount of RMB 4,396,229.94; seal up, distrain, freeze, auction, or sell the property of the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, in the amount of RMB 4,396,229.94. The enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo, was dissatisfied with this ruling and filed an enforcement objection application with the Yining City People's Court. On May 20, 2012, the Yining City People's Court rendered the Enforcement Objection Ruling (2012) Yi Zhi Yi Zi No. 31-1, dismissing the enforcement objection of the enforcement respondent, Li Zhengbo. Li Zhengbo was dissatisfied with this ruling and filed an application for reconsideration with the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region on June 5, 2012. On March 21, 2013, the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered the Enforcement Reconsideration Ruling (2012) Yi Zhou Zhi Fu Zi No. 00012, dismissing Li Zhengbo's application for reconsideration.

On April 8, 2013, Li Zhengbo filed a petition with the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, arguing that the breach of contract clause in the Civil Mediation Agreement (2010) Yi Min Chu Zi No. 1514 of the Yining City People's Court was not enforceable. The content of the mediation agreement was a modification of the original sales contract terms, reaching a new sales agreement through the court; Huaqiang Company, when applying for enforcement, did not provide evidence of Li Zhengbo's breach, whereas Li Zhengbo had commissioned the Yili Notary Public Office on June 26, 2010, to notarize Huaqiang Company's breach, proving Huaqiang Company's default facts, but the enforcement court did not accept this evidence; Huaqiang Company still owed him brick payments, and the party in breach during the performance of the mediation agreement was Huaqiang Company; directly determining Li Zhengbo's liability for breach of contract and the amount of liquidated damages in enforcement proceedings deprived Li Zhengbo of the right to appeal against the liability for breach and the amount of liquidated damages.

Upon review, the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region held that during enforcement, the parties had significant disagreements over who should bear liability for breach of contract in the performance of the Civil Mediation Agreement (2010) Yi Min Chu Zi No. 1514 of the Yining City People's Court, with both parties alleging that the other had breached. The enforcement court, by applying substantive law in enforcement proceedings to directly determine the parties' liability for breach of contract during the performance of the mediation agreement, exceeded the scope of enforcement review. The determination of such liability for breach should be resolved through litigation proceedings. The Enforcement Objection Ruling (2012) Yi Zhi Yi Zi No. 31-1 of the Yining City People's Court and the Enforcement Reconsideration Ruling (2012) Yi Zhou Zhi Fu Zi No. 00012 of the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region both exceeded the scope of enforcement rulings and were detrimental to protecting the lawful rights and interests of both parties, and should be revoked. Accordingly, on December 9, 2013, the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region rendered the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Xin Zhi Er Jian Zi No. 148, revoking the above two rulings.

The petitioner, Huaqiang Company, being dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Xin Zhi Er Jian Zi No. 148 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, filed a petition with this Court, arguing: 1. The High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region directly rendered a ruling revoking the Enforcement Objection Ruling (2012) Yi Zhi Yi Zi No. 31-1 of the Yining City People's Court and the Enforcement Reconsideration Ruling (2012) Yi Zhou Zhi Fu Zi No. 00012 of the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region without granting the petitioner the right to make statements and defenses, which violates the judicial principles of fairness, impartiality, and openness. 2. The ruling of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region had problems in the application of law. This case is a dispute over a sales contract. For a contract established in accordance with the law, the parties shall fully perform it. According to Article 19 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Work of Civil Mediation by People's Courts: "When the conditions of the guarantee clause or the clause on assuming civil liability determined by the mediation agreement are fulfilled, and a party applies for enforcement, the people's court shall enforce it in accordance with the law." The "conditions of the guarantee clause or civil liability" in that article all involve substantive civil law and include a process in which one party performs and the other party accepts performance. If the party who is to perform first fails to perform its obligation, the other party may apply to the court for compulsory enforcement without the need for further civil litigation before enforcement. In the mediation agreement of this case, the performance of the parties has a sequential order: Li Zhengbo supplies the goods, and Huaqiang Company receives the goods and pays the price as agreed. If Li Zhengbo fails to supply, Huaqiang Company may apply to the court for enforcement. Li Zhengbo's defense that Huaqiang Company did not give him notice to supply is untenable. First, assuming Huaqiang Company failed to perform the mediation agreement, Li Zhengbo could have taken measures such as deposit or applying for enforcement to perform, but he did not. Second, when Huaqiang Company applied for Li Zhengbo to perform the obligation of supplying bricks, Li Zhengbo immediately applied to the court for retrial, requesting revocation of the mediation agreement, and failed to perform the supply obligation. Third, at the time Huaqiang Company applied for enforcement, the price of building bricks had risen significantly, far exceeding the price determined by the mediation agreement. In summary, Huaqiang Company requests the revocation of the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Xin Zhi Er Jian Zi No. 148 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and the affirmation of the Enforcement Objection Ruling (2012) Yi Zhi Yi Zi No. 31-1 of the Yining City People's Court and the Enforcement Reconsideration Ruling (2012) Yi Zhou Zhi Fu Zi No. 00012 of the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

The respondent, Li Zhengbo, argued that the petition of Huaqiang Company is unfounded and should be dismissed. The main reasons are: 1. Li Zhengbo did not breach the contract. The content of the mediation agreement was clearly a modification of the 2009 sales contract, providing for the other party to pick up the goods, settlement methods, and liability for breach. Li Zhengbo had been performing in accordance with the contract. The other party, in order to raise the brick price, did not pick up bricks, causing the brick kiln stock to accumulate and preventing normal production, which is evidenced by notarization. 2. The key issue of this case is whether the mediation agreement is enforceable. Generally, mediation agreements set out rights and obligations very clearly without dispute. However, the mediation agreement in this case is an agreement on the rights and obligations of both parties. Only if one party breaches will liquidated damages be payable. Who breached the contract is a matter of significant dispute and should not be directly determined in enforcement proceedings. The mediation agreement is not suitable for direct enforcement.

Upon review, this Court holds that a legally effective mediation agreement not only confirms the content of the rights and obligations agreement reached by the parties on a voluntary and lawful basis, but also constitutes a legally enforceable instrument. According to Article 18 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the legal instrument submitted for enforcement shall have a subject matter for performance, and the enforcement subject matter and the enforcement respondent shall be clear. Therefore, the content determined by a legally effective instrument that may be subject to compulsory enforcement must be of a nature capable of being performed. If one party fails to perform in accordance with the determined content, the other party may apply to the people's court for compulsory enforcement in respect of that determined content. Therefore, when accepting an enforcement case, the people's court shall first examine whether the applicant's claim for the creditor's right exists, that is, it has the authority to examine whether the mediation agreement or other legal instrument is enforceable. Such examination primarily includes verifying whether the legal instrument has taken legal effect, whether the obligor has performed the obligation within the time limit determined by the legal instrument, and whether the conditions for compulsory enforcement determined by the legal instrument are clear. As for this case, the main body of the mediation agreement has two principal aspects. First, the parties have reciprocal obligations to perform: the defendant, Li Zhengbo, is obliged to supply 13.5 million sintered porous bricks to the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, and the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, is obliged to pay the price at the unit price of RMB 0.36 per brick. Thus, in respect of the reciprocal performance obligations determined by the mediation agreement, the mediation agreement has content for performance, and this case is one with enforcement content. When one party fails to perform in accordance with the content determined by the mediation agreement, the other party may apply to the people's court for enforcement. Second, there are the provisions on liability for breach of contract. The provisions on liability for breach are reflected in four clauses: Clause 1 provides that when the stock of bricks in each kiln exceeds one ring, the plaintiff shall pay RMB 0.015 for each excess brick; Clause 2 provides that if the defendant, Li Zhengbo, is unable to complete the monthly supply of bricks as agreed, he must make up the shortfall in the following month, and if the shortfall is still not made up in the following month, he shall compensate the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, at RMB 0.29 per brick for the shortfall; Clause 3 provides that the plaintiff, Huaqiang Company, shall settle accounts with the defendant, Li Zhengbo, on the 30th day of each month and pay the full amount for the bricks purchased that month within five working days, and for overdue payment, a penalty of 0.05% per day shall be borne; Clause 5 provides that both parties shall strictly perform the above agreement, and if the plaintiff fails to pay as agreed, it shall bear a penalty of 30% of the unpaid portion, and if the defendant fails to supply sufficient bricks, in addition to compensating the plaintiff at RMB 0.29 per brick, he shall also bear a penalty of 30% of the shortfall. Accordingly, because the mediation agreement does not specify the liability to be borne when one party has already breached, it is necessary to determine the certainty of the liability for breach as agreed in the mediation agreement. This is not a matter that should have been resolved in the litigation of the case but was not, nor can it be resolved through the retrial procedure. Moreover, the party in this case, Li Zhengbo, has already applied for retrial to the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, but both applications were dismissed for failing to meet the conditions prescribed by law. The obligation to pay arising from the liability for breach of contract by both parties, as determined in the mediation agreement of this case, depends on future events, i.e., whether and to what extent the parties have breached the agreement during the performance of the effective mediation agreement. Such an obligation constitutes a new substantive dispute over rights and obligations that arises in connection with new facts occurring after the conclusion of the case. It is not a simple factual determination, and direct determination in the enforcement proceedings lacks procedural legitimacy and necessary procedural safeguards. In order to more effectively protect the lawful rights and interests of all parties, the parties should be permitted to resolve the matter through a separate action. The reason argued by Huaqiang Company that the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region erred in the application of law is not sustainable. The conclusion of the Enforcement Ruling (2013) Xin Zhi Er Jian Zi No. 148 of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region is not erroneous and should be upheld. By reference to Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and pursuant to Article 129 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is ruled as follows:

The petition of Yining Huaqiang New Building Materials Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

This ruling shall take legal effect upon service.

Presiding Judge: He Dongning

Acting Judge: Xue Guizhong

Acting Judge: Xiang Guohui

December 2, 2014

Court Clerk: Liu Wei

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

He Dongning, Senior Judge: Born in 1966, Master of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2011.
